description: We’re the Meteor Rizzlers from Kerala, India, a team of developers from Rajagiri School of Engineering and Technology passionate about space exploration and solving complex problems. This year, we’re exploring SPHEREx data to uncover patterns and changes across the universe. Combining AI, scientific data, and interactive visualization, we aim to make astronomical observations easier to explore and understand.
summary:
SphereXPLORER is an interactive platform that brings the universe closer through immersive astronomical exploration and scientific visualization.

Built to make complex astronomical data easier to understand, it allows users to explore the sky, inspect celestial objects, and investigate their spectral properties through dedicated interactive tools. But it goes beyond simply displaying data.

With 3D visualizations, multi-view astronomical inspection, spectral analysis, and cross-epoch exploration through the Time Machine, users can examine the universe from different perspectives and uncover connections that might otherwise go unnoticed.

The platform combines scientific depth with an intuitive, story-driven interface. Every section encourages discovery, making the experience engaging rather than overwhelming.

Our vision is simple: turn complex astronomical observations into opportunities for discovery. By bringing data, visualization, and exploration together, SphereXPLORER aims to make astronomical research more accessible to researchers, students, and anyone curious about the universe.
details:
SphereXPLORER is designed to turn NASA's vast SPHEREx infrared survey into an interactive environment for astronomical exploration and citizen science.

At its core, the platform connects with the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA) to retrieve genuine SPHEREx observation metadata and calibrated Level 2 FITS images. Users can enter custom Right Ascension (RA) and Declination (Dec) coordinates, search for known celestial objects, or explore curated targets such as Barnard's Star, WISE 0855, Epsilon Indi B, RW Aurigae and R Draconis.

The platform is organized into several interconnected scientific workspaces:

  • Sky Explorer: An interactive all-sky atlas that allows users to navigate celestial regions, inspect coordinates and compare different astronomical survey layers.
  • Object Explorer: Provides detailed information about celestial objects, their observations, positions and available scientific data.
  • Spectral Explorer: Opens up SPHEREx's 102 infrared spectral channels, allowing users to investigate wavelength-dependent features and explore the molecular signatures of astronomical sources.
  • Time Machine: One of the platform's central features. It transforms genuine multi-epoch observations into an interactive time-lapse, with playback, blinking, side-by-side comparisons and difference imaging to help users identify changes in the sky.
  • Discovery Lab: Brings together image stacking, source detection, cross-epoch analysis and a discovery journal.
  • Missions: Introduces guided scientific activities and interactive learning experiences for newcomers.

Scientific reliability is a major consideration. Rather than relying on generated astronomical imagery, SPHEREXPLORER processes authentic FITS data using celestial coordinate transformations, WCS reprojection and calibrated image processing. Catalogue-predicted positions are distinguished from actual source detections, and unavailable observations or insufficient evidence are reported transparently.

Technology and Development

The frontend is developed using React 19, TypeScript, Vite and Tailwind CSS, with Three.js powering interactive 3D experiences, including a model of the SPHEREx spacecraft. Aladin Lite provides astronomical sky visualization.

The backend uses Python and FastAPI, supported by Astropy, Photutils, Reproject and PyVO for astronomical data retrieval, FITS processing, astrometry, image alignment and source detection. NASA/IPAC IRSA provides the primary SPHEREx data source, while Gaia DR3 and other astronomical catalogues provide additional reference information.

We also integrated Driver.js to provide guided walkthroughs, making the scientific tools approachable even for users without an astronomy background.

Creativity, Benefits and Intended Impact

What makes SPHEREXPLORER different is the way it combines scientific functionality with an immersive exploration experience. Instead of presenting users with complicated datasets and expecting them to understand everything independently, we created a platform that guides them through the process of exploring, comparing and interpreting astronomical observations.

We considered scientific accuracy, accessibility, performance, data availability, usability and the needs of both beginners and experienced astronomy enthusiasts throughout development.

Our ultimate goal is to make astronomical discovery more accessible and collaborative. By giving people intuitive tools to examine how the sky changes over time, SPHEREXPLORER aims to encourage citizen-science participation and help more people contribute to exploring the universe.
